title: Late Breaking Results: Automatic Anomaly Detection Method in Physical Unclonable Functions using Data Mining Techniques
problem: PUF-based security systems require distinguishing legitimate PUFs from those that are tampered, defective, or invalid; existing approaches lack systematic methods for detecting anomalies and security violations.
motivation: PUF deployment for hardware security requires robustness against tampering and manufacturing defects; anomaly detection mechanisms are underexplored and critical for practical security.
method: The approach uses data mining—a technique for finding patterns in data—to extract rules describing how legitimate Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs: unique, unchangeable hardware identifiers) normally behave. It then compares new or suspicious PUFs against these learned patterns to detect anomalies: significant deviations that indicate tampering, manufacturing defects, or counterfeiting. By systematically identifying when a PUF doesn't match expected behavior, the system catches security compromises automatically.
key_novelty: Using data mining to automatically detect when PUFs deviate from patterns of legitimate chips, catching tampering and defects.
contributions: Data mining methodology for characterizing valid PUF behavior patterns
Rule-based anomaly detection framework for tampering and invalidity detection
Experimental validation demonstrating tampering identification capability
limitations: Limited evaluation details due to late-breaking status; scalability across diverse PUF types not discussed.
